Name: Visible Scene Radiance
Description: Ambient visible-light radiance reflected from the apartment scene into the OAK-D Lite colour camera aperture.
Notes: Not stated in the repository; inferred from the fact that a ColorCamera node is configured at 1080p with a 416x416 preview. Units are the physical quantity, not a repository value.

Name: Dog Reflected Visible Radiance
Description: Visible light reflected from Billie's body into the OAK-D Lite colour camera, the physical basis of COCO-class dog detection.
Notes: Inferred physical precondition for the implemented detector. DT-OAK-01 in the results document confirms live detection of the real dog.

Name: Stereo Scene Radiance
Description: Visible/near-IR radiance reaching the OAK-D Lite left and right 400p mono imagers, the physical input to on-device stereo disparity.
Notes: Inferred from the configured stereo pair. Also configured in the bench publisher (billiebot_sensor_tests/oakd/oakd_bench_publisher.py).

Name: Near-IR and Visible Scene Radiance
Description: Combined near-infrared and visible radiance entering the Pi Camera 3 NoIR, which has no IR-cut filter.
Notes: The specifications document states the missing IR-cut filter lets near-IR leak into all three Bayer channels. No IR illuminator exists (see Planned IR Illumination signal).

Name: Active 850 nm IR Illumination
Description: Near-infrared scene illumination that the NoIR night-vision path requires but that no fitted emitter currently provides.
Interface: IR LED board on 5 V accessory rail
Notes: Explicitly a known hardware gap: the design document says the NoIR camera has no emitter and proposes an 850 nm LED board switched by an Arduino GPIO + MOSFET. No pin, driver, or code exists in the repository.

Name: Lidar Laser Emission
Description: Rotating infrared laser pulse train emitted by the RPLidar A1 into the apartment for time-of-flight/triangulation ranging.
RateBasis: Continuous physical interaction; emitter timing not stated in repository
Notes: Inferred from the presence of a configured RPLidar A1 driver. The repository configures only the serial port, baud, frame_id, angle_compensate and scan_mode -- no optical parameters.

Name: Lidar Range Return
Description: Backscattered laser energy from apartment surfaces returning to the RPLidar A1 receiver, from which per-beam range is derived.
Notes: Inferred physical counterpart of the emission signal. The repository contains no lidar firmware or optical model.

Name: Dog Body Thermal IR Radiance
Description: Long-wave infrared radiance emitted by Billie's body and received by the MLX90640 32x24 thermopile array.
Notes: Inferred from the implemented 30-40 degC warm-blob gate and SYS-PER-3. Bench test DT-THM-01 demonstrated warm-target detection to 1.5 m.

Name: Scene Thermal IR Radiance
Description: Background long-wave infrared radiance from apartment surfaces filling the non-dog pixels of the MLX90640 array.
Notes: Inferred: every pixel of the published 32FC1 frame is a temperature, so the background scene must be radiating into the array.

Name: Dog Bark Acoustic Pressure
Description: Airborne acoustic pressure wave produced when Billie barks, whines or howls, incident on the ReSpeaker microphone ports.
Notes: Inferred physical origin of the classified event. Test DT-AUD-01 in the results document records a live Billie bark producing a 0.992-confidence Animal/Dog classification.

Name: Ambient Acoustic Pressure
Description: General apartment sound field (speech, appliances, impulses) incident on the ReSpeaker array, the source of LOUD_NOISE events and of false positives.
Notes: UT-AUD-01 recorded ambient, speech and impulse conditions; speech and impulse exceeded the clipping threshold.

Name: Speaker Acoustic Output
Description: Status chime or spoken phrase radiated from the 3 W speaker into the apartment; rate-limited for dog welfare.
RateBasis: Event-driven; goals rejected within min_interval_sec (10 s default)
SourceLocation: goal_callback() rate limit lines 48-56; aplay invocation ~line 105
Notes: speaker_node plays WAV files via 'aplay -D plughw:0,0'. Volume is clamped to max_volume (0.5). SYS-PLT-6 reserves the speaker for status chimes only in the MVP. The physical radiation itself is inferred from the implemented playback path.

Notes: Die temperature, not a room-air measurement in the metrological sense; the firmware treats it only as a plausibility-checked companion to pressure.

Name: Earth Magnetic Field

Notes: The firmware header notes NDOF places the magnetometer in the fusion loop. BLK-13 in the bench test plan flags motor and speaker magnetics as a distortion risk and offers IMUPLUS as an alternative mode.

Name: Chassis Specific Force

SourceLocation: sampleImu() ACC_DATA_X_LSB 0x08, lines 415-422 and file header lines 24-29
Notes: Deliberately includes gravity (register 0x08, not VECTOR_LINEARACCEL 0x28), because the EKF sets imu0_remove_gravitational_acceleration. A compile-time static_assert enforces this.

Name: Chassis Angular Rate
Description: Body-frame angular rate of the chassis transmitted through the structure to the BNO055 gyroscope.
Notes: Firmware converts 16 LSB/dps to rad/s before transmission.

Name: Pi Thermal I2C Bus
Description: Physical I2C bus 1 on the Raspberry Pi 5 carrying MLX90640 frame reads.
RateBasis: Bus clock not configured in the repository
Notes: thermal_node declares i2c_bus and i2c_address parameters but the real-mode code calls board.I2C() and never reads them (thermal_node.py lines 28-29 vs 56) -- the parameters are declared and unused. The specifications document quotes 400 kHz as the device capability but the repository sets no clock. Receiver context: (address 0x33).

Name: BNO055 Orientation Register Data
Description: Fusion quaternion, gyroscope, accelerometer and calibration-status registers read from the BNO055 over I2C.
RateBasis: Timer period in source code (IMU_PERIOD_US 20000 us)
Notes: Read via a hand-rolled transaction-checked bnoRead() rather than the Adafruit library, because getQuat()/getVector() discard the transaction result and would return zeros on a NACK. Compile-time static_asserts pin the register addresses and the little-endian sign decode.

Name: BNO055 Magnetometer Register Data
Description: Three-axis magnetometer vector read from the BNO055 over I2C.
RateBasis: Timer period in source code (MAG_PERIOD_US 100000 us)
Notes: Uses the Adafruit getVector() path rather than bnoRead(), so a failed transaction here is not detected the way the IMU path detects one. Gated on g_bno_ok. Compile-time switch ENABLE_MAGNETOMETER can drop this record.

Name: BMP280 Pressure and Temperature Register Data
Description: Compensated pressure and temperature read from the BMP280 over I2C.
RateBasis: Timer period in source code (BAROMETER_PERIOD_US 500000 us)
Notes: Oversampling is set explicitly (x2 temperature, x16 pressure, filter x16, 63 ms standby) so the device conversion time is bounded against the 2 Hz emission slot. Implausible samples are counted and dropped, never transmitted.

Name: MLX90640 Thermal Frame Data
Description: 768-element (32x24) calibrated temperature frame read from the MLX90640 over I2C.
RateBasis: Sensor refresh configured in source code (RefreshRate.REFRESH_8_HZ)
Notes: This is the SENSOR refresh rate (8 Hz), deliberately distinct from the 4 Hz ROS publication rate of /thermal/image. The node polls getFrame() on its own 4 Hz timer, so roughly half the sensor frames are never read.

Name: NoIR CSI-2 Image Stream
Description: Raw Bayer/RGB888 frames transported from the Pi Camera 3 NoIR to the Raspberry Pi 5 over the MIPI CSI-2 link.
RateBasis: Derived from the node capture timer (publish_rate_hz 5.0); the camera's own frame rate is not configured unless frame_duration_us is set
Notes: capture_array() is pulled by the ROS timer, so the 5 Hz figure is the read rate rather than a configured sensor frame rate. build_camera_config() can optionally set FrameDurationLimits but defaults to a sentinel meaning 'do not touch'.

Name: OAK-D USB3 Device Link
Description: XLink stream over USB3 carrying spatial detections and, when enabled, RGB and depth preview frames from the OAK-D Lite to the Jetson.
RateBasis: Derived from the host output-queue poll rate (publish_rate_hz 5.0)
Notes: Inference runs on the OAK-D's RVC2, not the Jetson GPU. udev rule 99-billiebot.rules grants non-root access by matching vendor 03e7 alone because the device re-enumerates across product IDs while booting its firmware.

Name: Lidar USB-UART Link
Description: CP2102 USB-to-UART link carrying the RPLidar A1 measurement stream to the Jetson.
RateBasis: Link baud is 115200 (a bus rate, not a signal rate); scan rate is set by the lidar motor
Notes: The by-id path is used deliberately instead of ttyUSBn because enumeration order swaps between the lidar and the Arduino (GAP-20). No udev symlink rule is installed for it.

Name: ReSpeaker USB Audio Stream
Description: USB Audio Class isochronous stream carrying beamformed and raw microphone channels from the XVF3800 to the Raspberry Pi 5.
Notes: Rate here is the audio SAMPLE rate in Hz, not a message publication rate. Two channels are opened and classification_channel 1 is the one fed to YAMNet. The specifications document notes 6-channel firmware would also expose the four raw mics; the repository configures 2.

Name: XVF3800 Vendor Control Transfer
Description: USB vendor control requests used to read direction-of-arrival and to read/write the GPO and LED-effect resources on the XVF3800.
RateBasis: Event-driven for DoA reads; power-policy re-verification is on a 30 s timer
Notes: Read requests set wValue = 0x80 | command_id. All writes are volatile -- nothing is committed to device flash. X0D30 (mic mute) is read and reported but never written.

Name: XVF3800 Direction of Arrival Reading
Description: Beam azimuth and speech-detected flag returned by the XVF3800 DoA resource, used to populate AudioEvent.doa_deg.
RateBasis: Event-driven: read once per published /audio/events message
Notes: Valid range 0-359 deg. DT-AUD-02 requires proving the value is not fixed at zero; that test is listed as not performed in the bench results.

Name: XVF3800 GPO Power Policy State
Description: LED-ring power, onboard-amplifier enable and microphone-mute GPO pin states enforced and verified over USB.
Notes: Read-before-write: zero writes are performed when the device is already compliant. Strict mode makes an unverifiable policy a hard startup failure.

Name: I2S Audio Output Stream
Description: I2S PCM audio from the Raspberry Pi 5 to the MAX98357A class-D amplifier.
RateBasis: Unknown; the repository plays WAV files through ALSA 'plughw:0,0' and configures no I2S parameters
SourceLocation: BDD-04 'amp : MAX98357A I2S amp'; IBD-01 c11
Notes: speaker_node shells out to 'aplay -D plughw:0,0'; nothing in the repository confirms that device maps to the MAX98357A rather than another ALSA card. sounds_dir defaults to empty, so real playback would fail until it is configured.

Name: Amplified Speaker Drive
Description: Class-D amplified analog output driving the 3 W speaker voice coil.
Notes: Appears only in the architecture documents. No amplifier gain, impedance, or speaker part number is given beyond '3 W speaker'.

Name: Motor Nano Serial Link
Description: Bidirectional USB-serial link between the Jetson and the Motor Nano carrying the ASCII command/response protocol.
RateBasis: Link baud is 57600 (a bus rate); the command exchange itself runs at 30 Hz
Notes: README notes the design document said 115200 but the working firmware uses 57600. This is the safety-critical link: losing it for more than 500 ms must stop the motors (SYS-PLT-5).

Name: Wheel Velocity Command Frame
Description: ASCII 'm <left> <right>' frame carrying per-wheel target speeds in encoder counts per PID loop.
RateBasis: Timer period in source code (publish_rate_hz 30.0 drives update())
Notes: Sent unconditionally every update tick, including 'm 0 0' on command timeout or e-stop, which is also what keeps the Motor Nano's 500 ms watchdog fed. rad_s_to_counts_per_loop() converts using encoder_ticks_per_rev and pid_rate_hz.

Name: Encoder Count Query
Description: ASCII 'e' request asking the Motor Nano for the current cumulative encoder tick totals.

Name: Encoder Count Reply
Description: Space-separated cumulative left and right encoder tick totals returned by the Motor Nano.
RateBasis: Derived from serial loop timing: one reply per 'e' request at 30 Hz
Notes: Cumulative totals, not deltas; base_bridge differences them. Sign is applied host-side via left_encoder_sign / right_encoder_sign.

Name: Encoder Reset Command
Description: ASCII 'r' frame zeroing both encoder accumulators on the Motor Nano at bridge start-up.
RateBasis: Event-driven: once at start-up when reset_encoders_on_start is true
Notes: Acknowledged with 'OK'; the bridge retries up to five reads before giving up silently.

Name: Battery ADC Query
Description: ASCII 'a <pin>' frame asking the Motor Nano to sample the battery-divider analog input.
Notes: battery_pin defaults to 0 (A0).

Name: Battery ADC Count Reply
Description: Raw 10-bit ADC count of the battery divider returned by the Motor Nano.
RateBasis: Derived from serial loop timing: one reply per 'a' request at 1 Hz
Notes: Converted host-side as V = adc * 5.0 / 1023.0 * battery_divider_ratio (6.0). In mock mode MockSerial returns a constant 429 counts (~12.58 V), which means battery-triggered SAFE mode can never fire in mock.

Name: Serial Heartbeat Watchdog Timeout
Description: Motor Nano autonomous motor cutoff when no serial command arrives within the AUTO_STOP_INTERVAL window.
RateBasis: Event-driven: fires 500 ms after the last received command
Notes: firmware/README.md documents this as a REQUIRED CHANGE from the stock 2000 ms to 500 ms, satisfying SYS-PLT-5. Because the Motor Nano firmware is not in this repository, there is no evidence in-repo that the change has been applied. base_bridge's 30 Hz command cadence keeps it fed in normal operation.

Name: Sensor Nano Serial Link
Description: USB-serial link from the Sensor Nano to the Jetson carrying CRC-framed ASCII telemetry records.
RateBasis: Link baud is 115200 (a bus rate); aggregate offered load is documented at ~58% of the link
Notes: Each record is terminated '*XXXX\n' where XXXX is the CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE hex. The firmware self-checks crc16('123456789') == 0x29B1 at boot. Status is Test/Bench Only because no production bringup launch file starts the sensor_nano_bridge; the firmware header calls itself 'production-candidate'.

Name: IMU Telemetry Record
Description: Quaternion, gyroscope, accelerometer and BNO055 calibration levels in one CRC-framed line.
DataType: float quaternion + float[3] gyro + float[3] accel + uint8[4] calibration
Notes: Fields are lossless against each sensor's own quantum: 5 decimals quaternion, 4 gyro, 3 accel. A failed I2C transaction drops the whole sample rather than shipping zeros. Parsed by billiebot_sensor_tests/sensor_nano/protocol.py, which shares the CRC implementation with the firmware.

Name: Magnetometer Telemetry Record
Description: Three-axis magnetometer vector in one CRC-framed line.
Notes: Transmitted in microtesla rather than tesla to avoid eight decimals of fixed-point text; the bridge scales to tesla. Parsed by billiebot_sensor_tests/sensor_nano/protocol.py, which shares the CRC implementation with the firmware.

Name: Battery ADC Telemetry Record
Description: Mean raw ADC count of the battery divider accumulated since the previous record.
Notes: One conversion is accumulated per loop iteration, so each record averages hundreds of samples without delaying the IMU path. The firmware deliberately carries no divider ratio, ADC reference or threshold -- the Jetson bridge owns every conversion. Parsed by billiebot_sensor_tests/sensor_nano/protocol.py, which shares the CRC implementation with the firmware.

Name: Barometer Telemetry Record
Description: Plausibility-checked BMP280 pressure and temperature in one CRC-framed line.
Notes: Samples outside 30-110 kPa or -40 to 85 degC are counted and dropped rather than transmitted. Parsed by billiebot_sensor_tests/sensor_nano/protocol.py, which shares the CRC implementation with the firmware.

Name: Sensor Nano Status Record
Description: Peripheral health flags, BNO055 fusion mode and cumulative error counters.
DataType: uint8 flags + uint8 mode + uint16 counters
Notes: Fusion mode is read back from the chip rather than echoing the compile-time #define, so a modified build cannot misrepresent a captured run. Counters cover I2C errors, IMU read errors, BMP errors, reinits and dropped IMU records. Parsed by billiebot_sensor_tests/sensor_nano/protocol.py, which shares the CRC implementation with the firmware.

Name: Sensor Nano Sequence Counter
Description: Monotonic 32-bit counter shared by every record type so a dropped frame of any type is a single global discontinuity.
RateBasis: Event-driven: one increment per emitted record (aggregate ~68 records/s)
Notes: UT-IMU-01 gates on ut_imu_01_max_sequence_discontinuity_fraction 0.001.

Name: Sensor Nano Uptime Timestamp
Description: Firmware micros() value carried in every record and surfaced as an uptime figure in diagnostics.
Notes: Explicitly never interpreted as ROS or Unix epoch time; it rolls over every ~71.6 minutes. The bridge stamps messages with the ROS clock at the moment the line is received in the reader thread.

Name: Sensor Nano CRC Self-Check Error Line
Description: Plain 'E,crc16_self_check_failed' line emitted at boot if the firmware CRC implementation disagrees with the canonical check value.
RateBasis: Event-driven: at most once, during setup()
Notes: Not a member of RECORD_TYPES, so the bridge's parser rejects it as malformed and counts it -- the failure surfaces as a parse error rather than as a decoded diagnostic.

Name: Target Wheel Angular Velocity
Description: Per-wheel angular-velocity setpoints derived from the commanded body twist by the differential-drive inverse kinematics.
RateBasis: Consumed by the 30 Hz update() timer; produced on each /cmd_vel callback
Notes: Uses wheel_separation 0.298 m and wheel_radius 0.034 m, both flagged as unmeasured in MEASURE_ME.md. Included because it is the architectural translation point between body-frame command and wheel-frame command. Receiver context: (internal to the node: cmd_callback -> update).

Name: Encoder Tick Delta
Description: Per-cycle difference in cumulative encoder counts, the primitive from which all wheel motion is derived.
Notes: Converted to radians with rad_per_tick = 2*pi/encoder_ticks_per_rev. Receiver context: (internal: update -> odometry integration).

Name: Wheel Angular Velocity Estimate
Description: Software estimate of each wheel's angular velocity, computed from the tick delta and elapsed time.
Notes: Distinct from the physical wheel angular velocity signal; this is the estimate, subject to encoder_ticks_per_rev calibration error. Receiver context: (internal: feeds /joint_states).

Name: Integrated Odometric Pose
Description: Dead-reckoned x, y and yaw obtained by integrating the differential-drive kinematics over each cycle.
Notes: Uses the midpoint-yaw arc approximation when |dyaw| >= 1e-12. Yaw is unbounded (never wrapped). Receiver context: (internal: feeds /odom and optional odom->base_link TF).

Name: Battery Voltage Estimate
Description: Pack voltage reconstructed from a raw ADC count using the divider ratio and ADC reference.
Notes: V = adc * 5.0 / 1023.0 * 6.0. The same conversion exists independently in the Sensor Nano path (battery_metrics.adc_to_volts) with the reference voltage and ratio exposed as parameters. Both are nominal until BLK-07/BLK-08 measurements are taken. Receiver context: (internal: feeds /battery_state).

Name: Battery Health Classification
Description: Mapping of pack voltage onto BatteryState power-supply status and health enums at the 10.5 V and 9.9 V thresholds.
Notes: BLK-06: low voltage is mapped onto POWER_SUPPLY_HEALTH_COLD, which is a temperature health code. Per-cell voltages are synthesised by dividing pack voltage by cell count rather than measured. The Sensor Nano bridge deliberately does neither. Receiver context: (internal: populates /battery_state).

Name: Quaternion Frame Convention Transform
Description: Optional documented world-frame rotation applied to the BNO055 fusion quaternion before publication, plus renormalisation.
RateBasis: One transform per received IMU record (50 Hz)
Notes: Default 'bno055_native' publishes the chip quaternion unchanged; 'nwu_to_enu' applies a +90 deg yaw change. BLK-14: the chip's fusion world frame is not yet verified on this hardware, which is why native is the default. Receiver context: (internal: feeds /imu/data).

Name: IMU Covariance Assignment
Description: Provisional diagonal covariances attached to orientation, angular velocity and linear acceleration in the published Imu message.
RateBasis: One assignment per published IMU message (50 Hz)
Notes: BLK-15: explicitly NOT a characterised accuracy claim. Non-zero because robot_localization treats an all-zero covariance as unknown and substitutes a destabilising tiny default. Receiver context: (internal: populates /imu/data).

Name: Serial Parse Statistics
Description: Running counts of good records, CRC failures, malformed records, queue drops and overlong-line discards on the Sensor Nano link.
Notes: Also written to a bag-independent exports/ file so a run stays diagnosable when the bag is missing or truncated. Receiver context: (internal: feeds diagnostics and the stats export file).

Name: Spatial Detection Coordinates
Description: On-device stereo-derived 3-D coordinates of a detection, converted from DepthAI millimetres to metres in the camera optical frame.
Notes: Depth thresholds are set to 100-5000 mm and the bounding-box scale factor to 0.5. Depth is aligned to CAM_A so boxes map correctly into the depth image.

Name: Normalised Bounding Box
Description: DepthAI normalised [0,1] detection box scaled to 416x416 pixel coordinates and clamped to the frame.
Notes: Appendix B-11: the previous int(det.xmin) truncated every real box to approximately zero because the coordinates are always in [0,1]. Preview size is fixed at 416 px. Receiver context: (internal: populates DogDetection3D).

Name: Thermal Temperature Frame Array
Description: 768-element float temperature list read from the MLX90640 and reused as the buffer for both image publication and blob detection.
Notes: Receiver context: (internal: feeds /thermal/image and blob detection).

Name: Warm Blob Statistics
Description: Centroid, pixel area, maximum and mean temperature of pixels falling inside the 30-40 degC dog window.
DataType: float centroid + int area + float temps
Notes: A single global threshold, not connected-component labelling, so two separate warm objects merge into one 'blob'. DT-THM-01 recorded a 7.84% baseline false-positive blob rate against an empty scene. Receiver context: (internal: populates ThermalBlob).

Name: Audio Ring Buffer Waveform
Description: Mono float32 waveform window pulled from the continuous-capture ring buffer for each classification cycle.
Notes: continuous_capture:=false restores the original blocking sd.rec() path, documented in-code as the confirmed non-functional 2 Hz-cadence bug and kept only as an explicit rollback. Receiver context: (internal: feeds YAMNet inference).

Name: Audio Energy Level
Description: RMS energy of the classification window in dB, used as the gate before YAMNet inference and reported in AudioEvent.energy_db.
Notes: Gate threshold energy_threshold_db defaults to -40.0 dB. dB reference is 20*log10(RMS) of the float32 waveform, i.e. dBFS-like, not SPL. Receiver context: (internal: energy gate and event payload).

Name: YAMNet Class Scores
Description: 521-class TFLite score vector produced by YAMNet, reduced to a top label and score.
Notes: Labels are mapped through YAMNET_DOG_CLASSES to BARK/HOWL/WHINE, with anything else above the confidence threshold becoming LOUD_NOISE. Class-map file must sit next to the .tflite model or the node exits. Receiver context: (internal: maps to AudioEvent type).

Name: Fused Evidence Window
Description: Ten-second sliding buffers of visual detections, thermal blobs, audio events and dog poses used to classify behavioural state.
Notes: window_sec 10.0, hysteresis_sec 3.0. Buffers are bounded (maxlen 100 visual, 50 each for the others). Receiver context: (internal: fuse_and_publish).

Name: Dog Stress Proxy
Description: Heuristic welfare indicator derived from bark rate (and, per design, retreat motion) carried in DogState.
Notes: SYS-EXT-4 reserves this field for the future Behavior AI. The design document describes it as bark rate plus retreat motion; only the bark-rate component is visible in the implementation. Receiver context: (internal: populates DogState.stress_proxy).

Name: Behavior AI Context Vector
Description: Reserved raw feature vector carried in DogState for a future contextual-bandit policy.
Notes: SYS-STL-3 / SYS-EXT-3: the interface exists so a learned classifier or bandit can be dropped in without a message change. No consumer reads it in the MVP beyond logging. Receiver context: (internal: populates DogState.context).

Name: Behavior AI Context Vector
Description: Reserved raw feature vector carried in DogState for a future contextual-bandit policy.
Notes: SYS-STL-3 / SYS-EXT-3: the interface exists so a learned classifier or bandit can be dropped in without a message change. No consumer reads it in the MVP beyond logging. Receiver context: (persisted as context_json).

Name: Mission Mode State
Description: Current operational mode of the IDLE / PATROL / INVESTIGATE / TRACK_OBSERVE / RETURN / SAFE state machine.
SourceLocation: Mode IntEnum lines 29-35; tick() timer line 98
Notes: Startup mode is IDLE, so an operator /set_mode call is required to begin patrolling. INVESTIGATE and RETURN are reachable only via /set_mode and have no behaviour attached (BRINGUP_LADDER_ANALYSIS.md). Receiver context: (internal: drives tick() behaviour).

Name: Behavior Tree Policy Decision
Description: Action decision emitted by the PolicyDecision behavior-tree node; the MVP ObserveOnlyPolicy always returns OBSERVE.
Notes: GAP: the C++ BT nodes are compiled into billiebot_bt_nodes but no launched process loads behavior_trees/billiebot_main.xml or registers them, so this node is never ticked. The implemented mission logic is the Python state machine in mission_controller.py instead. Same applies to battery_guard_node and estop_guard_node.

Name: Battery Guard Condition
Description: Behavior-tree condition that fails when pack voltage falls below the 10.5 V safe threshold.
Notes: Never ticked -- see Behavior Tree Policy Decision. Threshold default 10.5 V matches SYS-PLT-2.

Name: E-Stop Guard Condition
Description: Behavior-tree condition that fails while the e-stop is engaged.
Notes: Never ticked. Compounding GAP-8: mission_controller has an _estopped flag but no subscription or service client that could ever set it, so the e-stop never reaches mission logic by any route.

Name: Dog Event Record
Description: Persisted (timestamp, state, confidence, position, room, snapshot path, context, action, outcome, stress proxy) tuple written on every state transition.
RateBasis: Event-driven on state transition, plus a periodic write every 60 s
Notes: WAL journal mode for crash safety (SYS-STL-4). The (context, action, outcome) columns satisfy SYS-EXT-3 for future bandit bootstrap; in the MVP 'action' always defaults to OBSERVE.

Name: Room Assignment
Description: Map-frame dog position resolved to a named room using configured rectangular boundaries.
Notes: rooms_config defaults to an empty string in cognition.yaml, so with the shipped configuration every event resolves to 'unknown'. MEASURE_ME.md flags rooms.yaml as placeholder data pending an apartment map.

Name: Daily Activity Summary
Description: Aggregated per-day sleep/rest/active durations, bark counts, timeline and room histogram rendered to Markdown/HTML.
RateBasis: Event-driven: the node checks a 60 s timer and generates once per day at generate_hour/minute (23:55)
Notes: Satisfies SYS-RPT-1. The 60 s figure is the poll interval, not the report rate; the report itself is daily.

Name: Snapshot Image File
Description: JPEG snapshot captured on a dog-state transition and referenced from the event record.
RateBasis: Event-driven: on state transition when enable_snapshots is true
SourceLocation: enable_snapshots parameter line 62; snapshot_dir creation lines 71-72
Notes: GAP-9 in DISCREPANCY_RESOLUTION_PLAN.md concerns real snapshots; dog_logger subscribes only to /billie/state and has no image subscription, so the source of the snapshot pixels is not established in the repository.

Name: Velocity Command
Description: Commanded body-frame linear and angular velocity for the differential-drive base.
Notes: Single motion sink: base_bridge is the only subscriber. Speed caps SYS-NAV-5 (0.3 m/s transit, 0.15 m/s near dog) are not enforced in base_bridge; nav2_params holds the velocity limits.

Name: Velocity Command
Description: Open-loop reverse velocity published directly by the Retreat action server, bypassing Nav2.
RateBasis: Event-driven: published only while a Retreat goal is executing
Notes: Second publisher on /cmd_vel. retreat_speed default 0.1 m/s (mission.yaml). Same SignalID as the Nav2 flow because it is the same logical velocity command on the same topic.

Name: Velocity Command
Description: Manual teleoperation twist from the operator's host computer over the robot WLAN.
Notes: SYS-PLT-4 requires teleoperation, and MBSE IBD-03 c1 lists teleop as a /cmd_vel publisher, but no teleop node, launch entry, or dependency exists in billiebot_ws. Present in documentation only.

Description: Dead-reckoned pose and twist integrated from wheel encoder ticks, in the odom frame.
Notes: The EKF is the sole consumer since the GAP-4 resolution; Nav2 reads /odometry/filtered instead. Covariance is left at its default zeros. Orientation carries yaw only (z, w).

Notes: Joint names come from left_joint_name / right_joint_name parameters (left_wheel_joint, right_wheel_joint).

Notes: BLK-02: this is the currently-implemented battery publisher and it reads the MOTOR Nano's A0. The Sensor Nano bridge publishes the same topic from the Sensor Nano's A0. Running both would create duplicate publishers with different semantics; the bench plan contract-tests that no Sensor Nano launch starts base_bridge.

Name: Dog Found Flag
Description: Boolean asserted or cleared every detector cycle according to whether a dog was seen in that frame.
Notes: GAP-12: /dog/found has TWO publishers. This one publishes both true and false at 5 Hz; dog_locator publishes only true. mission_controller therefore sees an interleaved stream, which BRINGUP_LADDER_ANALYSIS.md identifies as a cause of PATROL/TRACK_OBSERVE flapping.

Name: Dog Found Flag
Description: Boolean asserted whenever a detection is successfully transformed into the map frame.
RateBasis: Event-driven: one message per successfully transformed detection (bounded by the 5 Hz detection rate)
Notes: Publishes true only -- it never emits false on loss, which is the second half of GAP-12.

Name: Dog Map Pose
Description: Dog position transformed from the camera optical frame into the map frame via tf2.
RateBasis: Event-driven: one message per detection that passes the confidence gate and transforms successfully (bounded by 5 Hz)
Notes: min_confidence 0.5. TF lookup timeout is 0.1 s and a TransformException is only logged at debug level, so failures are silent. Orientation is fixed at identity.

Notes: 640x360 at JPEG quality 70. Explicitly documentation of shipped defaults, never a threshold -- analysis always reads the raw topics. Companion topics /bench/oakd/depth/preview/compressed (320x200) and /bench/oakd/points_preview (stride 16, 2 Hz) follow the same pattern. Receiver context: (Foxglove visualisation).

RateBasis: Event-driven: one output per received /thermal/image frame (bounded by 4 Hz)

RateBasis: Event-driven: one status per received /noir/image frame (bounded by 5 Hz)

Name: Audio Classifier Status
Description: Per-cycle classifier telemetry: energy, gate outcomes, top label and score, inference duration and XVF3800 power-policy state.
Notes: Published every processing cycle whether or not an event was emitted, precisely so the 2 Hz cadence can be measured independently of the sparse /audio/events topic. DT-AUD-01 requires 1.8-2.2 Hz here; the bench results record that this sustained measurement was NOT performed.

Name: Audio Capture Diagnostics
Description: Resolved device identity, overflow count and blocks written during a bench WAV capture.
RateBasis: Timer period in source code (diag_timer at 1.0 s)
Notes: UT-AUD-01 support node. Writes one WAV of capture_duration_sec (3.0 s default) per launch.

Name: Sensor Nano Diagnostics
Description: Serial-link parse statistics plus BNO055/BMP280 health, fusion mode, error counters and calibration levels.
Notes: Carries the BNO055 calibration levels, which have no home in sensor_msgs/Imu. UT-IMU-01 records them as informational metrics that never gate the result.

Name: Battery Raw ADC
Description: Raw averaged ADC count behind each published BatteryState voltage, for divider and reference calibration.
Notes: Published from the same B record in the same callback immediately after the BatteryState. That ordering is the documented pairing invariant UT-BAT-01 relies on: the Nth ADC sample is the raw count behind the Nth voltage.

Name: Magnetic Field
Description: Three-axis magnetometer vector converted from microtesla to tesla.
RateBasis: Timer period in firmware (MAG_PERIOD_US 100000 us); one message per 'M' record
Notes: The publisher is only created when publish_magnetometer is true, deliberately, so an advertised-but-silent /imu/mag can never imply a feed that does not exist. Covariance is left all-zero. No live node subscribes. Receiver context: (offline, via rosbag2).

Name: Barometric Pressure
Description: Absolute atmospheric pressure from the BMP280.
RateBasis: Timer period in firmware (BAROMETER_PERIOD_US 500000 us); one message per 'P' record
Notes: variance is set to 0.0, the sensor_msgs convention for unknown. No live node subscribes; UT-IMU-01 gates the values against a 30-110 kPa band. Receiver context: (offline, via rosbag2).

Name: Barometric Temperature
Description: Die temperature reported by the BMP280 alongside pressure.
RateBasis: Timer period in firmware (BAROMETER_PERIOD_US 500000 us); one message per 'P' record
Notes: Published from the same 'P' record and the same callback as the pressure message, sharing its stamp. No live node subscribes. Receiver context: (offline, via rosbag2).

Name: Synthetic Battery State
Description: Synthetic voltages driving the production mission controller across the exact 10.5 V SAFE boundary.
RateBasis: Event-driven: held per test case for case_hold_sec
Notes: A THIRD publisher of /battery_state, bench-only. BLK-05: at exactly 10.5000 V the requirement says SAFE and the production strict '<' comparison does not, so that case is expected to fail until the inequality is fixed. The test plan states the failure is the deliverable.

Name: Inter-Host DDS Traffic
Description: All ROS 2 topic, service and action traffic exchanged between the Jetson and the Raspberry Pi over the robot WLAN.
RateBasis: Aggregate of every cross-host topic; not independently configured
Notes: Multicast is disabled because Wi-Fi multicast discovery is unreliable; peers are static. The IP addresses are placeholders the README tells the operator to update. ParticipantIndex auto with MaxAutoParticipantIndex 32.

Name: Inter-Host DDS Traffic
Description: Return direction of the cross-host ROS 2 traffic, chiefly perception, audio and cognition topics from the Pi to the Jetson.
RateBasis: Aggregate of every cross-host topic; not independently configured
Notes: Node-to-host allocation comes from jetson.launch.py (nav2, OAK-D, dog locator, mission) and pi.launch.py (thermal, NoIR, audio, cognition).

Name: Operator DDS Session
Description: ROS 2 traffic between the robot and the operator's host computer for visualisation, teleoperation and e-stop.
SourceLocation: IBD-00 IF_WiFi_DDS; Section 5.1 Operator UI row
Notes: SYS-PLT-4. The router (GL-SFT1200) is modelled in the Support Segment, outside the rover boundary. The host must load the same CycloneDDS peer list for discovery to work.

Name: Daily Report HTTP Response
Description: Rendered daily activity report served over HTTP from the Raspberry Pi to the operator's browser.
RateBasis: Event-driven: one response per operator HTTP request
Notes: Satisfies SYS-RPT-2. Binds 0.0.0.0, so it is reachable from anywhere on the WLAN. Falls back to raw Markdown in a <pre> block when the markdown package is unavailable.

RateBasis: Event-driven: operator action per rotation step
Notes: Labels are flat, x_plus_90, x_minus_90, y_plus_90, y_minus_90, z_plus_90 for UT-IMU-01. The commanded-rotation gates are computed from body-frame relative rotations, which are invariant to the world-frame convention choice.

Name: Recorded Bag Data
Description: rosbag2 recording of the bench topics, the authoritative artefact every offline analyser reads.
RateBasis: Event-driven: mirrors the recorded topics' own rates
Notes: Raw topics remain the only authoritative source for rosbag2, the rate monitor and every analysis CLI; the compressed preview topics are explicitly excluded from that role.

Name: Motor Nano Encoder Count
Description: Cumulative signed tick totals maintained inside the Motor Nano by the quadrature decode interrupt service routines.
RateBasis: Event-driven: incremented per encoder edge; the rate tracks wheel speed
Notes: This is the distinct MCU-internal stage between the electrical channel A/B pulse trains and the serial 'e' reply. The Motor Nano's own firmware is not in this repository, so the evidence is the reference sketch that firmware/README.md implies the board runs. Receiver context: (internal: read by the 'e' command handler and the PID loop).

Name: Motor Nano PID Duty Output
Description: Per-motor duty value computed by the firmware velocity PID loop from the commanded and measured counts per loop.
RateBasis: Documented nominal (pid_rate_hz 30.0 in base_driver.yaml; the host converts to counts-per-loop against this figure)
Notes: The 30 Hz figure is the rate the HOST assumes when converting rad/s into counts per loop (base_bridge.rad_s_to_counts_per_loop). If the actual firmware PID rate differs, every commanded velocity is scaled by the ratio -- an unverifiable coupling while the Motor Nano firmware sits outside this repository. Sign of the duty selects the forward or backward PWM pin. Receiver context: (internal: written to the PWM outputs by setMotorSpeeds()).

Name: Motor Nano Command Parse
Description: Single-letter serial command dispatch inside the Motor Nano that routes 'm', 'e', 'r' and 'a' frames to their handlers.
RateBasis: Derived from serial loop timing: base_bridge issues 'm' and 'e' every 30 Hz cycle plus 'a' at 1 Hz
Notes: commands.h also defines o/p/s/t/u/w/x (raw PWM, ping, servo read/write, PID update, digital write, analog write) that base_bridge never issues. Those are latent interface surface, not active signals. Receiver context: (internal: command dispatch to motor, encoder and ADC handlers).

Name: Lidar Rotor Rotation
Description: Continuous rotation of the RPLidar A1 optical head that sweeps the beam through 360 degrees.
RateBasis: Continuous physical interaction; motor speed is not configured in the repository
Notes: Purely inferred from the device type. The rotor speed sets the scan rate, which is why /scan has no configured rate in this repository. No motor-control topic or parameter is exposed. Receiver context: (internal: the rotating optical assembly).

Name: MLX90640 Refresh Rate Configuration
Description: I2C register write setting the MLX90640 internal frame refresh rate at node start-up.
Notes: Sets 8 Hz sensor refresh against a 4 Hz ROS publication rate. The specifications document notes the Adafruit driver reaches roughly 16 Hz in practice against a 32 Hz theoretical limit, so 8 Hz is well inside the device envelope.

Name: BNO055 Mode Configuration
Description: I2C configuration writes placing the BNO055 into NDOF absolute-orientation fusion mode at boot and after a bounded recovery.
RateBasis: Event-driven: at setup() and on each bounded reinitialisation
Notes: Recovery is bounded: 25 consecutive failures trigger a re-begin, at most once per 5 s cooldown and at most 20 times total. begin() blocks for roughly a second, which is why the schedule is re-armed afterwards. The firmware leaves BNO055_UNIT_SEL at its power-on default, which is what makes the transmitted scale factors correct.

Name: BMP280 Sampling Configuration
Description: I2C configuration write selecting BMP280 oversampling, IIR filter and standby time at boot.
RateBasis: Event-driven: at setup() and on each bounded reinitialisation
SourceLocation: setSampling(MODE_NORMAL, X2, X16, FILTER_X16, STANDBY_MS_63) lines 601-605
Notes: Chosen explicitly rather than relying on reset defaults so the device conversion time is known and bounded against the 2 Hz emission slot. A dead BMP280 recovers independently of the BNO055 on the shared bus, by design.

Name: NoIR Camera Control Settings
Description: libcamera control writes for autofocus mode, lens position, exposure time, analogue gain and frame-duration limits.
RateBasis: Event-driven: applied once at camera configuration
Notes: Every parameter defaults to a sentinel ('' / False / -1 / None) meaning 'do not touch', so with the shipped configuration no controls key is emitted at all and real-mode capture behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged. Only a bench launch sets any of them.

Name: OAK-D Pipeline and Model Upload
Description: DepthAI pipeline description and the YOLOv8n .blob network uploaded to the OAK-D over USB at node start-up.
Notes: Real mode has no fallback: a missing or invalid blob exits non-zero so the launch supervisor surfaces the failure rather than the perception chain coming up green but blind. Parser settings (80 classes, coordinate size 4, IoU 0.5) must be set explicitly because DepthAI v2 defaults them to zero. model_path in perception.yaml points at an absolute developer path, /home/sean/billiebot/models/yolov8n_416.blob.

Name: XVF3800 Power Policy Write
Description: USB vendor control write clearing the LED-ring power GPO and disabling the onboard amplifier when the device is found non-compliant.
RateBasis: Event-driven: only when a read shows the device has reverted; zero writes when already compliant
Notes: Volatile only -- nothing is committed to device flash. X0D30 (microphone mute) is deliberately never written, only observed and reported. Strict mode turns an unverifiable policy into a hard startup failure rather than a silent power leak.

Name: Particle Cloud
Description: AMCL particle distribution published for operator inspection of localisation convergence.
RateBasis: Event-driven: published on each filter update
Notes: Standard AMCL output listed in the MBSE decomposition as part of the relocalisation surface. Not configured or referenced by any BillieBot-authored code. Receiver context: (operator visualisation).

Name: Nano USB Auto-Reset (DTR)
Description: DTR assertion when the host opens the serial port, which resets the Arduino Nano into its bootloader.
RateBasis: Event-driven: once per serial port open
Notes: The Sensor Nano bridge waits startup_settle_sec (2.5 s) and flushes the input buffer, so bootloader noise and truncated first records are discarded rather than counted as parser errors. base_bridge performs the equivalent flush without an explicit settle delay, which is an asymmetry between the two bridges.
